subject: Acme POC — next steps & eval methodology (recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@acmecorp.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC — next steps & eval methodology (recap)

Hi Emma + Raj —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the kickoff:

1) Key goals / success criteria (proposed)
- Accuracy on intent extraction >= 92% (macro-averaged)
- Mean response latency (p95) < 500ms under target traffic profile
- Hallucination rate (false facts per 1k responses) < 2
- QA pass rate on a human-reviewed sample >= 95%
- Cost target: <= $X per 1k tokens (we'll refine once we see sample load)

2) Recommended evaluation approach (high-level)
- Phase A (offline eval): small labeled dataset (1k-2k examples) for quick iteration and rubric-based grading. This gives a baseline metric set and surfacing of major failure modes.
- Phase B (online shadow / limited traffic): mirror ~5% of production traffic for 2 weeks to validate behavior on live inputs and measure latency/cost under load. Default is to run shadow only after offline baseline meets minimum thresholds.

3) Ownership / responsibilities
- Redwood (Dylan): handle data ingestion, offline eval scripts, metric dashboards, and shadow deployment config.
- Redwood (Marissa): customer coordination, kickoff, and weekly status.
- Acme (Emma / Raj): provide sample prompts, label set for offline eval, and signoff on final success criteria.

4) Timeline (proposed)
- Jul 29: receive labeled sample + prompt set from Acme
- Aug 5: complete offline eval and share rubric-scored results
- Aug 8-22: online shadow (if offline baseline passed)
- Aug 26: validation and remediation window
- Aug 30: final review and go/no-go decision

Attachments: acme_poc_success_criteria.xlsx (template), redwood_eval_rubric_v2.pdf (scoring rubric)

Please confirm the above and let us know if you prefer a different cadence for the shadowing phase (e.g., mirror vs. 5% routed traffic). If this looks good we'll schedule a kickoff for Aug 1 to align on data handoff.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

- For online shadow: we prefer mirror traffic to start if possible (so we see exact live inputs without risking routing). If mirror is difficult, routing 5% is OK but we need a clear rollback plan.

I've attached a short list of follow-up questions and our internal labeling guidelines (acme_poc_questions.docx).

Subject: Re: Acme POC — next steps & eval methodology (recap)

Emma / Raj —

Thanks for the quick response. A few concrete notes on how we propose to run the offline eval and what the shadow will look like operationally: 

Offline eval (Phase A) — design details
- Sample size: aim for 1,500 labeled examples (stratified by intent + edge-case bucket). That gives decent confidence intervals for accuracy/precision metrics.
- Holdouts: 80/20 train/validation split; we recommend a separate 200-example blind test set for rubric scoring.
- Grading rubric: we'll score on Accuracy, Relevance, Hallucination (binary flags), and Response Safety. Each category gets a numeric score; final pass/fail threshold is a weighted aggregate (we'll share weights and let Acme adjust). See attached redwood_eval_rubric_v2.pdf.
- Automation: we will run unit metric scripts and produce a report with confusion matrices, sample failure list, and suggested prompt fixes.

Online shadow (Phase B) — operational plan
- Mirror vs. routed: mirror is preferred — we record live inputs and responses without returning Redwood responses to end users. If routing 5% is the only option, we recommend starting with mirror for 3 days, then 5% routed for 1 week. 
- Traffic split: suggest mirror for initial validation; then 5% routed if metrics look stable.
- Rollback and fallback: immediate rollback via routing policy; we will configure automatic fallback to a smaller, well-tested model if hallucination thresholds spike or p95 latency exceeds agreed SLO.
- Observability: dashboards for per-route latency, error rate, hallucination flags, and per-batch cost.

Owners / timeline (operational)
- Dylan: build eval pipeline, metric dashboards, and shadow configuration (deadline Aug 5 for offline results; ready for shadow Aug 8).
- Marissa: kickoff owner and customer comms.
- Rachel: success criteria signoff and weekly checkpoints.

Action items for Acme
- Share labeled sample and labeling guidelines by Jul 29
- Confirm preferred shadow mode (mirror vs. 5% routed)
- Confirm any additional compliance checks for shadowed traffic (PII scrubbing)

I've attached an internal playbook (eval_pipeline_playbook.md) that outlines the scripts and expected outputs. Happy to walk through this at the kickoff.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.com
